questions.text: Under SPP 204-A, in how many arrangements can fulltime supervision services be provided?

options.text: One: through the CSG only
Two: dual capacity (architect as supervisor) or consulting architect only
Three: CSG, architect, or construction manager
Four: CSG, architect, contractor's superintendent, or independent inspector

rationale.a: CSG-only is just one of the two recognized arrangements.
rationale.b: Correct. SPP 204-A recognizes two arrangements: (1) dual capacity, where the architect of record also provides fulltime supervision, and (2) consulting architect only, where a separate architect/firm provides supervision services.
rationale.c: Three arrangements overspecifies. Construction management is covered under SPP 204-B.
rationale.d: Four arrangements is incorrect and mixes roles from different SPP documents.
rationale.correct: SPP 204-A provides for two arrangements: dual capacity (where the designing architect also supervises) and consulting architect only (where a separate professional provides supervision). Both require qualified CSG personnel.
rationale.takeaway: Two arrangements: dual capacity or consulting architect only.

questions.text: What type of report must the CSG prepare daily under SPP 204-A?

options.text: Weekly Progress Report (WPR)
Monthly Status Report (MSR)
Daily Inspection Report (DIR)
Construction Activity Log (CAL)

rationale.a: Weekly reports are too infrequent for fulltime supervision. SPP 204-A requires daily reporting.
rationale.b: Monthly reports are inadequate for the level of supervision SPP 204-A demands.
rationale.c: Correct. The CSG must prepare Daily Inspection Reports (DIRs) documenting all construction activities, inspections, issues, and decisions for each working day.
rationale.d: Construction Activity Log is not the term used in SPP 204-A. The specified document is the DIR.
rationale.correct: SPP 204-A requires the CSG to prepare Daily Inspection Reports (DIRs) for every working day. DIRs document construction activities, inspection findings, material deliveries, weather conditions, workforce count, and any issues or directives.
rationale.takeaway: CSG must prepare Daily Inspection Reports (DIRs) every working day.

questions.text: What minimum educational qualification is required for a CSG inspector under SPP 204-A?

options.text: A technical vocational diploma in construction
A Bachelor of Science in Architecture (BS Arch) degree
A master's degree in construction management
Any engineering degree from a CHED-recognized school

rationale.a: A vocational diploma is insufficient. SPP 204-A requires a professional degree.
rationale.b: Correct. A CSG inspector must hold a Bachelor of Science in Architecture (BS Arch) degree, ensuring professional competence in architectural supervision.
rationale.c: A master's degree is not required. The minimum is a BS Arch degree.
rationale.d: An engineering degree does not substitute for the BS Arch requirement for CSG inspectors under SPP 204-A.
rationale.correct: SPP 204-A requires CSG inspectors to hold a BS Architecture degree as a minimum qualification. This ensures inspectors have the architectural knowledge needed to verify that construction faithfully executes the architect's design intent.
rationale.takeaway: CSG inspector minimum qualification = BS Arch degree.

questions.text: What are the four scope areas of the Construction Supervision Group under SPP 204-A?

options.text: Design Review, Cost Estimation, Scheduling, Safety, ensuring all aspects of the project are aligned with the initial design intent and budget constraints
Quality Control, Evaluation, Daily Reports, Filing/Documentation
Site Preparation, Material Testing, Labor Management, Handover, focusing on the readiness of the site and the quality of materials used
Procurement, Logistics, Quality Assurance, Closeout, which includes the final inspection and approval of all project components

rationale.a: Design review and cost estimation are not CSG scope areas. These fall under Design Development and Construction Management.
rationale.b: Correct. The four CSG scope areas are: (1) Quality Control of construction work, (2) Evaluation of progress and performance, (3) Daily Reports on construction activities, and (4) Filing/Documentation of all records.
rationale.c: Site preparation and labor management are contractor responsibilities, not CSG scope areas.
rationale.d: Procurement and logistics are construction management functions under SPP 204-B, not CSG scope areas.
rationale.correct: The CSG's four scope areas under SPP 204-A are: Quality Control (ensuring construction matches specifications), Evaluation (assessing progress and contractor performance), Daily Reports (documenting daily activities and issues), and Filing/Documentation (maintaining organized construction records).
rationale.takeaway: CSG scope: Quality Control, Evaluation, Daily Reports, Filing.

questions.text: Under SPP 204-A, who hires the Construction Supervision Group (CSG), and to whom is the CSG answerable?

options.text: Hired by the Architect, answerable to the Owner only, ensuring that the architect's vision is executed while maintaining accountability to the client
Hired by the Owner, answerable to both the Owner and the Architect
Hired by the Contractor, answerable to the Owner only, which can lead to potential conflicts of interest if not properly managed
Hired by the Owner, answerable to the Architect only, allowing the architect to maintain control over the construction process

rationale.a: The Architect does not hire the CSG. The employment relationship is between the Owner and the CSG.
rationale.b: Correct. Under SPP 204-A, the CSG is hired by the Owner but is answerable to both the Owner and the Architect, establishing a dual accountability structure.
rationale.c: The Contractor does not hire the CSG. This would create a conflict of interest in supervision.
rationale.d: While the Owner hires the CSG, the CSG is answerable to both the Owner and the Architect, not just the Architect.
rationale.correct: The CSG is hired by the Owner but maintains dual accountability to both the Owner and the Architect. This structure ensures the Owner's investment is protected while the Architect's design intent is faithfully executed during construction.
rationale.takeaway: CSG: hired by Owner, answerable to both Owner AND Architect.

questions.text: What is the key difference between SPP 202 construction phase services and SPP 204-A fulltime supervision?

options.text: SPP 202 requires weekly visits; SPP 204-A requires monthly visits
SPP 202 requires periodic site visits; SPP 204-A requires daily 8-hour supervision
SPP 202 covers structural inspection; SPP 204-A covers architectural inspection only
SPP 202 is for private projects; SPP 204-A is for government projects only

rationale.a: The frequency distinction is incorrect. SPP 202 is periodic (not specifically weekly) and SPP 204-A is daily.
rationale.b: Correct. SPP 202 provides for periodic site visits during construction, while SPP 204-A mandates daily 8-hour continuous on-site supervision by the CSG.
rationale.c: Both cover all aspects of architectural work, not divided by structural vs. architectural inspection.
rationale.d: Both SPP 202 and 204-A apply to all project types, not distinguished by ownership.
rationale.correct: The fundamental difference is intensity: SPP 202 requires periodic site visits (checking progress at intervals), while SPP 204-A mandates daily 8-hour continuous on-site supervision by qualified CSG inspectors. SPP 204-A is separately compensated.
rationale.takeaway: SPP 202 = periodic visits; SPP 204-A = daily 8-hour continuous supervision.

options.text: Project Manager
Site Engineer
Clerk-of-Works
Building Inspector

rationale.a: Project Manager is a separate role covered under SPP 206, not the precursor to the CSG.
rationale.b: Site Engineer is an engineering role, not the traditional architectural supervision role that evolved into the CSG.
rationale.c: Correct. The CSG concept evolved from the traditional Clerk-of-Works role, modernizing and professionalizing on-site architectural supervision.
rationale.d: Building Inspector is a government regulatory role, not the traditional predecessor of the CSG.
rationale.correct: The Construction Supervision Group (CSG) under SPP 204-A evolved from the traditional Clerk-of-Works role. The modernization expanded the scope from a single clerk to a professional group, added formal qualifications, and structured the reporting framework.
rationale.takeaway: CSG evolved from the traditional Clerk-of-Works role.

questions.text: What does Article 1723 of the Civil Code, as referenced in SPP 204-A, establish regarding architect liability?

options.text: 5-year warranty period with individual liability, covering only specific defects
10-year warranty period with joint liability, ensuring shared responsibility among parties
15-year period with solidary liability among engineer, architect, and contractor
20-year period with limited liability for architects only, focusing on design errors

rationale.a: 5 years with individual liability is incorrect. Article 1723 establishes a longer period and broader liability.
rationale.b: 10 years with joint liability is incorrect on both counts — the period is 15 years and the liability is solidary (joint and several).
rationale.c: Correct. Article 1723 establishes a 15-year period of solidary (joint and several) liability among the engineer, architect, and contractor for structural defects.
rationale.d: 20 years is incorrect, and liability under Article 1723 extends to engineers and contractors, not just architects.
rationale.correct: Article 1723 of the Civil Code establishes solidary (joint and several) liability among the engineer, architect, and contractor for a period of 15 years from project completion. This means each party can be held liable for the entire amount of damages for structural defects.
rationale.takeaway: Article 1723: solidary liability, 15-year period, engineer + architect + contractor.

questions.text: Under SPP 204-A, should the CSG assume the contractor's superintendent responsibility?

options.text: Yes, the CSG supervises all contractor personnel, ensuring compliance with project specifications
Yes, but only for quality-related matters, focusing on adherence to design standards
No, the CSG shall NOT assume the contractor's superintendent responsibility
No, unless the Owner specifically requests it in writing, providing a formal directive

rationale.a: The CSG does not supervise contractor personnel. That is the superintendent's role.
rationale.b: Even for quality matters, the CSG monitors and reports but does not assume the superintendent's management role.
rationale.c: Correct. SPP 204-A explicitly states that the CSG shall NOT assume the contractor's superintendent responsibility. The CSG monitors and reports; the contractor's superintendent manages construction operations.
rationale.d: There is no exception for Owner request. The prohibition is absolute under SPP 204-A.
rationale.correct: SPP 204-A explicitly prohibits the CSG from assuming the contractor's superintendent responsibility. The CSG's role is to monitor, inspect, and report — not to manage or direct the contractor's workforce or operations.
rationale.takeaway: CSG must NOT assume contractor's superintendent responsibility — monitor only.
